transcription.original_script:
№ 2
Сероцкѣ
Состоялось въ Посадѣ Сероцкѣ пятнадцатаго (двадцать седьмаго Янва-
ря, тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года въ одиннадцать
часовъ утра. — Явился лично Моисеева Закона Шмуль Ма-
еръ Цитроновичъ, торговецъ, Двадцать осьми лѣтъ отъ роду,
здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ жительствующій, въ присутствіи свидѣтелей
Моисеева Закона Абрама Борнштейна, работника, сорока се-
ми лѣтъ отъ роду и Ицка Розенберга работника тридцати
шести лѣтъ отъ роду, здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ жительствующихъ,
и предъявилъ намъ младенца мужескаго пола, объявляя, что
онъ родился здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ Двадцать шестаго Декабря (Седь-
маго Января, тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ шестаго (седьмаго)
года, въ шесть часовъ по полудни, отъ законной его жены Ха-
ва Рухля урожденной Зоферштейнъ, Двадцать пяти лѣтъ
отъ роду. Младенцу этому при обрѣзаніи дано имя Лейбъ.
Актъ сей объявляющему и свидѣтелямъ прочитанъ, а
затѣмъ объявляющимъ, свидѣтелями, а также нами
подписанъ. S. Cytronowicz
A. Borensztejn   Jcek Rozenberg
Содержащій Акты Гражданскаго Состоянія
transcription.translation: No. 2. Serock. It took place in the Posad of Serock on the fifteenth (twenty-seventh) of January, one thousand eight hundred seventy-seven, at eleven o'clock in the morning. There appeared in person Szmul Majer Cytronowicz, of the Mosaic faith, merchant, twenty-eight years of age, residing here in Serock, in the presence of the witnesses Abram Borensztejn, of the Mosaic faith, laborer, forty-seven years of age, and Icek Rozenberg, laborer, thirty-six years of age, both residing here in Serock, and he presented to us an infant of male sex, declaring that it was born here in Serock on the twenty-sixth of December (the seventh of January), one thousand eight hundred seventy-six (seventy-seven), at six o'clock in the afternoon, of his lawful wife Chawa Ruchla née Zofersztejn, twenty-five years of age. This infant was given the name Lejb at the circumcision. This act was read to the declarant and the witnesses, and was thereupon signed by the declarant, by the witnesses, and also by us. S. Cytronowicz. A. Borensztejn. Icek Rozenberg. Keeper of the Registers of Civil Status.

notes: CONTRADICTS THE BATCH BRIEF, which pins target.language = "pl". The act is written in Russian in pre-reform orthography. Recorded from the ink.
The only Latin-script writing on the act is in the three autographs of the signature block; the clerk's own text is entirely Cyrillic.
Read at 6x over source (2200,1187,590,58). The -надцатаго tail and the пят- opening are both legible here, unlike act 1.
Parenthesised second day-word; the month name is split across the line 1/2 break and the excerpt is quoted across the break as inked.
Gap check: 15 to 27 January is 12 days, correct for 1877.

Working out that this clerk writes the Gregorian side as 'двадцать + ordinal' rather than as a single -надцатаго word corrected an earlier misreading of the same slot; the дцат cluster in двадцать is easy to mistake for the дцат in -надцатаго.
Two day-words physically inked; the closing parenthesis is not clearly formed, which is this clerk's habit.
Straddles the line 2/3 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Line-break split in the second given name (Ма- / -еръ). Read at 6x over source (2330,1280,460,60) and (1665,1328,560,60).

The surname Цитроновичъ is firm and is corroborated by the Latin-script autograph 'S. Cytronowicz' in the signature block, read at 4.2x over source (1700,1930,1090,130). The autograph initial S also supports Шмуль for the first given name.
Majer versus Szaer for the second name is the residual doubt; Ма- is preferred because the initial is a two-stroke М rather than a three-hump Ш.
Standard declarant-is-father construction; the word отецъ is not used. No midwife or illegitimacy wording.
Read at 6x over source (1665,1310,700,45). Unlike act 1, the declarant slot here does carry a trade word.
Двадцать is firm; the unit word is not. Read at 6x over source (2200,1330,590,58).
осьми is preferred because the token shows a round o, then s, then a tall ь loop, then m and i; шести would open on a three-hump ш instead.
Resident in the posad itself, unlike act 1's village declarant; agrees with the margin annotation.
Same person as the declarant.
Either reading is consistent with the mother's stated age of 25.
Body text read at 3.4x and 6.5x over source (1985,1424,500,58). On the body text alone the surname initial looked like a looped Л or М and the reading Лейзермана was first proposed.

The signature block settles it: the second autograph reads 'A. Borensztejn', which matches the given name Абрама and supplies a Б initial that the body loop also permits. The -нштейна tail agrees with the body between the two readings.
The rejected first reading is kept as an alternative rather than deleted, since the body ink alone does not compel Борнштейна.
The -ботника skeleton is legible at 6.5x; the initial р is partly taken from the slot. Distinct in shape from the сапожника of act 1.

notes: Age phrase split across the line 6/7 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Plural residence phrase covering both witnesses.
Inked in the genitive. Corroborated by the third autograph, read as 'Jcek Rozenberg' at 4.2x; the Latin J here stands for I, as was normal in this period's Polish-script Jewish signatures.
Not the same Rozenberg as act 1's witness, whose given name is Fajbisz.
Read at 6x over source (1900,1471,620,58). Excerpt carries the following word so that it is uniquely locatable in the transcription.
Split across the line 7/8 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Read at 6.5x over source (2330,1795,460,60). The -ейбъ tail with its terminal ъ after б is unambiguous; the capital Л carries a flourish but the shape is clear.
Corroborated by при обрѣзаніи in the naming slot and by the masculine что онъ родился.
Read at 5x over source (2100,1608,690,58). Julian side falls in 1876, which the doubled year-words on line 11 record.
Parenthesised, split across the line 10/11 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Gap check: 26 December Julian to 7 January Gregorian is 12 days, correct.
Both day-words inked, and the year is doubled as семьдесятъ шестаго (седьмаго).
по полудни, so six in the afternoon rather than the morning; read at 4.4x over source (1665,1702,900,58).
Born in the posad; agrees with the margin annotation Сероцкѣ.
A double given name split across the line 12/13 break: the line ends Ха- and the next opens ва Рухля. Quoted across the break as inked.
The single-name alternative Ruchla is retained in case the Ха- fragment belongs to a word other than a name, though no other reading of the slot presents itself.
Not the same woman as act 1's Хава, whose maiden name and age both differ.
Highest-value field on the act. Read at 5.5x and 8x over source (2090,1750,240,58).

The -ферштейнъ tail is firm. The initial is a single large loop with a descender, which in this hand serves З, С and Д alike, and the following vowel is equally soft between о and а, so the head of the surname is forked three ways.
Deliberately not resolved to the most familiar spelling.
Read at 6.5x over source (2380,1750,410,60).

notes: No illiteracy clause on this act; all three parties signed.
Autographs: 'S. Cytronowicz' on the closing line, then 'A. Borensztejn' and 'Jcek Rozenberg' below. All three are Latin script, in contrast to act 1 where one signature is Cyrillic.
The signature block was the decisive cross-check for both witness surnames and for the declarant's.
